findings.issue_text: P1: Lithuanian totpStep1 in messages_lt.properties replaced with Italian text and zh_CN totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese, showing wrong-language UI to users

P2: santizeAnchors uses a Matcher created over the original 'value' string while 'value' is reassigned via replaceFirst inside the loop, causing stale offsets that can skip or double-handle tags (false positives/negatives)

P2: verifySafeHtml throws a bare RuntimeException when the English counterpart file is missing/unreadable instead of falling back or raising MojoExecutionException, crashing the build with an unhelpful error
P2: Double HTML unescaping in normalizeValue (source value and sanitizer output) creates asymmetric comparisons, false positives for escaped literal text, and weakens policy protection
P3: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, breaking the error contract expected by callers/tests

P3: HTML_TAGS regex only matches lowercase tags, so uppercase/mixed-case tags like
are classified as no-HTML, causing false flags on mirroring translations
P3: Encoding mismatch between Files.readString (UTF-8) and PropertyResourceBundle parsing (falls back to ISO-8859-1) can decode the same file differently, causing spurious or missed HTML findings

santizeAnchors() uses position-insensitive value.replaceFirst(...) removal, so translations repeating the same anchor in a different order remove the wrong instance and cause spurious build failures (P3, confidence 75)

Encoding mismatch: verify() reads files with Files.readString() (UTF-8) while verifySafeHtml() uses PropertyResourceBundle (ISO-8859-1 default), so byte sequences could decode differently and hide smuggled HTML (P2, confidence 50)

HTML_TAGS regex <[a-z]+[^>]*> only matches lowercase tag names and fails for tags with '>' inside quoted attributes, so the containsHtml gate and the sanitizer disagree about what counts as HTML, causing inconsistent policy application (P3, confidence 50)

normalizeValue() hardcodes regex stripping for keys templateHelp, optimizeLookupLookupHelp and error-invalid-multivalued-size on both translation and English values; content adjacent to stripped markers plus unescapeHtml4() round-trip sensitivity to double-escaping (&lt;) is the most plausible sanitizer bypass path (P2, confidence 50)

POLICY_SOME_HTML allowlist is incomplete for email templates (no , , ,
,
variants), so legitimate future translations will fail the build, as shown by the hand-patched locale files in this PR (P3, confidence 75)

English-file path derivation via replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and _[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties is fragile: files outside resources-community or locales with digits (e.g. es_419) get a wrong English path or self-gating, and a self-gating bypass allows HTML injected into a translation whose English lookup fails (P2, confidence 75)
verifySafeHtml() throws raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException for I/O errors, producing a stack trace instead of a build diagnostic (P3, confidence 100)

File read twice per properties file: verify() reads the file with Files.readString and then verifySafeHtml() re-opens the same file with a new FileInputStream and parses it again into a PropertyResourceBundle, causing double I/O and double parse per file

Quadratic-ish anchor stripping in santizeAnchors: each loop iteration calls Pattern.quote + replaceFirst which compiles a fresh regex and rebuilds the string, and replaceFirst only removes the first occurrence so duplicate identical anchor tags (e.g., two identical <a href="{0}"> links) are never removed and matcher/value indices desynchronize

Per-key regex re-execution in normalizeValue: replaceAll calls with static patterns (CLAIM\.<[A-Z]*>, <Extensions>, {n,choice,...}, and the quoted RTL style pattern) are re-compiled and executed for every key in every bundle even when the key cannot match; should pre-compile Pattern constants and gate on key name

English-file path derivation regex is fragile: replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties", "_en.properties") can mis-derive paths for directories containing _+suffix patterns, and any miss causes a FileNotFoundException wrapped in RuntimeException aborting the whole verification run; for _en files it needlessly re-derives and reopens its own path
IOException or unresolvable English fallback file in verifySafeHtml() throws bare RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, killing the build with poor diagnostics
containsHtml uses lowercase-only regex <[a-z]+[^>]*>, so uppercase tags like <B> or <A HREF=...> are classified as no-HTML, causing legitimate translations to be stripped and flagged as Illegal HTML

Wrong-language content in translation files: messages_lt.properties totpStep1 replaced with Italian text, and messages_zh_CN.properties totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese text, not caught by the new verifier
santizeAnchors() mutates value while Matcher still references the original string, causing offset misalignment and removal of the wrong anchor tag occurrence in multi-anchor messages
Error-path inconsistency: verifySafeHtml uses RuntimeException while verify() uses MojoExecutionException for the same failure class
Email-file detection via file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email") is fragile and can silently strip RTL style attributes from all keys in unrelated paths containing 'email'

No test covers the positive path where the English source contains allowed HTML and translation legitimately contains the same HTML (POLICY_SOME_HTML branch and anchor pass-through), so a bug stripping/rejecting legitimate HTML would only surface as a build failure

Workaround/normalization paths in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, error-invalid-multivalued-size special cases, email RTL style stripping, double unescapeHtml4, '<!-- -->' removal) have zero test coverage and may silently break when the OWASP sanitizer library is upgraded

Error path where a translation file has no _en counterpart throws a raw RuntimeException (instead of MojoExecutionException) and is untested, risking a build crash with an unhelpful exception on unmapped paths

Wrong-language translations shipped: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text and zh_CN totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese text; the theme-verifier HTML check cannot detect wrong-locale content and no test or review gate covers it

Duplicate-key test assertion loosened from Matchers.contains to Matchers.hasItem, so the test passes even if the new HTML check emits spurious additional messages on the duplicate-keys fixture, masking defects

New pluralization MessageFormat choice pattern ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}) in messages_en.properties and account-ui equivalent is untested and never rendered with 0/1/2+ values to verify correct output

Brittle path-based coupling: English source file located by regex string-munging of getAbsolutePath() ('resources-community'→'resources', '_xx.properties'→'_en.properties'), silently no-ops or crashes if file lives outside expected layout — path derivation should come from mojo configuration instead

Key-specific special cases hardcoded in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHack, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) whitelist exact keys inside generic HTML verification, growing list and breaking silently on key renames — should use declaration-based mechanism

Asymmetric entity unescaping (unescape before sanitize and again after) can mask real problems: benign values with literal & or numeric entities may normalize differently and produce false 'Illegal HTML' failures; fragile escape/unescape dance already leaking into per-value hacks like <!-- --> removal
verifySafeHtml throws bare RuntimeException('unable to read file...') instead of wrapping in MojoExecutionException like existing verify() error handling, surfacing as unhandled runtime crash

containsHtml regex HTML_TAGS '<[a-z]+[^>]*>' misses uppercase tags like ,

,
, causing false POLICY_NO_HTML positives depending on case — use case-insensitive flag

santizeAnchors uses replaceFirst on Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), removing first occurrence of identical tag which may not be the matched occurrence — position-insensitive logic in a position-sensitive check; method name also misspelled ('santizeAnchors')
POLICY_SOME_HTML / POLICY_NO_HTML are non-static, package-visible mutable instance fields re-initialized per verification instead of private static final constants

HTML can be smuggled inside {n,choice,...} clauses for allowlisted keys: normalizeValue replaces ChoiceFormat clauses with '...' in both translation and English source before sanitization, so dangerous markup in choice branches passes the sanitized-vs-original comparison and is rendered at runtime (P1)
Same smuggled-content hole exists for templateHelp CLAIM.<[A-Z]*> and optimizeLookupHelp <Extensions> strips, though with narrower scope (P1)

Fragile English-file path derivation in verifySafeHtml: the greedy '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' regex is applied to the whole absolute path, so earlier underscores in CI workspace/home/temp dir paths get rewritten, producing a nonexistent path and crashing the build instead of degrading gracefully (P1)

verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the English properties file is missing/moved, aborting verification of all remaining checks instead of reporting a diagnostic; getEnglishValue fallback only handles missing keys, not missing files (P1)
Italian text committed into Lithuanian translation file messages_lt.properties, key totpStep1: wrong-language content shipped to users (P2)
Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式, 驗證碼) committed into the Simplified Chinese zh_CN file messages_zh_CN.properties, key totpStep1: locale/script mismatch (P2)

Path-based 'email' substring heuristic in normalizeValue strips style="direction: rtl;" from any file whose path merely contains 'email', allowing translators to inject RTL styles in unrelated files whose English source lacks them; broaden the anchor/attribute equality rule instead (P2)
Anchor-violation message in santizeAnchors omits the file name, making violations hard to localize across thousands of properties files (P3)
Method name misspelled as santizeAnchors instead of sanitizeAnchors (cosmetic) (P3)
verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException on I/O errors instead of MojoExecutionException, bypassing the plugin's error-handling convention and making failure messages inconsistent (P3)

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Lithuanian totpStep1 in messages_lt.properties replaced with Italian text and zh_CN totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese, showing wrong-language UI to users

P2: santizeAnchors uses a Matcher created over the original 'value' string while 'value' is reassigned via replaceFirst inside the loop, causing stale offsets that can skip or double-handle tags (false positives/negatives)

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, the `matcher` is created from the original `value`, but the loop only uses `matcher.group()` (the matched tag text), not match indices/offsets. Reassigning `value` via `replaceFirst(...)` does not affect `matcher.find()` progression in a way that would “skip or double-handle” tags due to stale offsets, because offsets are never used. The code may have other edge-case concerns (e.g., `replaceFirst` removes the first occurrence of the tag text, not necessarily the specific matched occurrence), but the stated stale-offsets mechanism is not verifiable from the diff and is largely a misread of how the code operates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: verifySafeHtml throws a bare RuntimeException when the English counterpart file is missing/unreadable instead of falling back or raising MojoExecutionException, crashing the build with an unhelpful error

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), reading the English counterpart file (englishFile) is wrapped in a try/catch that throws a new RuntimeException on IOException: `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e);`. Since verify() calls verifySafeHtml() unconditionally and does not catch RuntimeException (it only catches IOException from Files.readString), a missing/unreadable English file will crash execution with a bare RuntimeException rather than producing a MojoExecutionException or a graceful fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Double HTML unescaping in normalizeValue (source value and sanitizer output) creates asymmetric comparisons, false positives for escaped literal text, and weakens policy protection

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both the source value and the sanitized value are unescaped via `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(...)` (in `normalizeValue(...)` and again after `policy.sanitize(value)`), so the comparison is not “asymmetric” as claimed. Also, unescaping the sanitizer output is only used for equality comparison/reporting and does not “weaken policy protection” (the OWASP policy is applied before that unescape). While unescaping entities could change how escaped literals are interpreted, the finding’s stated effects (asymmetric comparison and weakened protection) are not supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, breaking the error contract expected by callers/tests

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()`, only `IOException` from `Files.readString(...)` is wrapped into `MojoExecutionException`. The newly added `verifySafeHtml()` instead catches `IOException` while reading `file`/`englishFile` and rethrows a raw `RuntimeException` (two `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")`). Because `verifySafeHtml()` is invoked outside the `try/catch` that wraps `IOException`, these `RuntimeException`s will escape `verify()` despite its `throws MojoExecutionException` contract, changing failure behavior for callers (including the Maven plugin).

adjudication_records.issue_text:
P3: HTML_TAGS regex only matches lowercase tags, so uppercase/mixed-case tags like
are classified as no-HTML, causing false flags on mirroring translations

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml(), HTML_TAGS is defined as Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") which only matches lowercase tag names. Since containsHtml(englishValue) controls whether POLICY_SOME_HTML vs POLICY_NO_HTML is used for the translation, an English source string containing uppercase/mixed-case HTML tags (e.g.,
,
) would be treated as containing no HTML, and the translation could then be incorrectly flagged as having “Illegal HTML” even if it mirrors the source. This is a correctness defect in the newly added verifier logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Encoding mismatch between Files.readString (UTF-8) and PropertyResourceBundle parsing (falls back to ISO-8859-1) can decode the same file differently, causing spurious or missed HTML findings

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()`, the file is read with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` (Java default UTF-8) for `verifyNoDuplicateKeys(contents)`, but `verifySafeHtml()` then loads the same `.properties` via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file))`, which uses the `PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` constructor (historically ISO-8859-1 semantics unless wrapped in a UTF-8 `Reader`). This creates an encoding inconsistency within the verifier introduced by the diff, and can cause the HTML safety logic to operate on differently-decoded text than other checks / the actual intended UTF-8 message content, potentially producing false positives/negatives for “Illegal HTML” comparisons.

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors() uses position-insensitive value.replaceFirst(...) removal, so translations repeating the same anchor in a different order remove the wrong instance and cause spurious build failures (P3, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), the code iterates over anchor tags found in the *original* `value` via `matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)`, but then mutates `value` inside the loop using `value.replaceFirst(...)` without rebuilding the matcher. Also, `replaceFirst` removes the first occurrence of the matched anchor substring in the current `value`, not the specific occurrence corresponding to the current `matcher.find()` position. With repeated/duplicated anchor tags (or multiple different anchors), this combination can remove a different instance than the one being iterated and/or make the verifier overly order/position sensitive, producing false “Didn't find anchor tag …” / “Illegal HTML …” failures for translations that contain the same anchors but arranged differently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Encoding mismatch: verify() reads files with Files.readString() (UTF-8) while verifySafeHtml() uses PropertyResourceBundle (ISO-8859-1 default), so byte sequences could decode differently and hide smuggled HTML (P2, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `verify()` reading the file via `Files.readString(file.toPath())`, which uses UTF-8 by default, while `verifySafeHtml()` loads the same `.properties` via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file))`, which uses the standard Java properties encoding (ISO-8859-1 with `\uXXXX` escapes). Since these message files clearly contain raw non-ASCII characters (many translations in the diff), the two code paths can decode the same bytes differently. That can cause `verifySafeHtml()` to sanitize/compare a mis-decoded string (false positives/negatives), undermining the intended HTML verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML_TAGS regex <[a-z]+[^>]*> only matches lowercase tag names and fails for tags with '>' inside quoted attributes, so the containsHtml gate and the sanitizer disagree about what counts as HTML, causing inconsistent policy application (P3, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml(), the new gate uses `Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which (a) only matches lowercase tag names and (b) stops at the first `>` character, even if it appears inside a quoted attribute value. Because this regex determines whether to apply POLICY_SOME_HTML vs POLICY_NO_HTML, it can misclassify an English source string as “no HTML” while the OWASP sanitizer still treats it as HTML, leading to inconsistent policy application and likely false-positive “Illegal HTML” findings for translations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: normalizeValue() hardcodes regex stripping for keys templateHelp, optimizeLookupLookupHelp and error-invalid-multivalued-size on both translation and English values; content adjacent to stripped markers plus unescapeHtml4() round-trip sensitivity to double-escaping (&lt;) is the most plausible sanitizer bypass path (P2, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show normalizeValue() applying key-specific regex replacements (for "templateHelp", "optimizeLookupHelp"—not "optimizeLookupLookupHelp"—and "error-invalid-multivalued-size") to both the translation and the derived English value before sanitization/comparison, and it unescapes HTML entities via StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(). However, the finding’s claimed “most plausible sanitizer bypass path” via adjacent stripped content and double-escaping (&lt;) is speculative and not demonstrably a defect from the shown logic: unescapeHtml4() is applied symmetrically and the sanitizer still runs on the resulting string, and treating escaped markup like "<script>" as plain text is not clearly a bypass of “illegal HTML” detection based on actual tags. No concrete, diff-grounded bypass is evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
POLICY_SOME_HTML allowlist is incomplete for email templates (no , , ,
,
variants), so legitimate future translations will fail the build, as shown by the hand-patched locale files in this PR (P3, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows email-related strings do include <a> tags, but the new verifier explicitly special-cases anchors via `santizeAnchors(...)`, allowing only anchor tags that exactly match the English source (it removes those anchors before applying the OWASP policy). Therefore the claim that POLICY_SOME_HTML “has no <a>” causing email templates to fail is not supported by the introduced logic. The remaining parts (e.g., <table>/<span>/<div> not allowed) are speculative “future translations” concerns and not evidenced as a defect by the diff; the PR appears intentionally restrictive (POLICY_SOME_HTML only allows br/p/strong/b).

adjudication_records.issue_text: English-file path derivation via replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and _[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties is fragile: files outside resources-community or locales with digits (e.g. es_419) get a wrong English path or self-gating, and a self-gating bypass allows HTML injected into a translation whose English lookup fails (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English bundle path is derived with `.replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This pattern excludes digits, so filenames like `messages_es_419.properties` would not be rewritten to `_en.properties`, yielding an incorrect `englishFile` path (either pointing to a non-existent file in `resources` after the `resources-community` swap, causing a RuntimeException, or potentially self-referencing if already in `resources`). This fragility is directly implied by the regex used in the diff. However, the specific claimed “bypass when English lookup fails” is less directly supported because missing English file load throws, and missing keys default to empty which enforces `POLICY_NO_HTML`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml() throws raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException for I/O errors, producing a stack trace instead of a build diagnostic (P3, confidence 100)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), only the Files.readString() path is wrapped into a MojoExecutionException, but verifySafeHtml() itself catches IOException when reading both the translated file and the derived English file and rethrows a raw RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). Since verifySafeHtml() is called inside the try block but not caught as IOException, this RuntimeException can escape verify() despite its declared throws MojoExecutionException, leading to an unstructured Maven failure/stack trace rather than a MojoExecutionException diagnostic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: File read twice per properties file: verify() reads the file with Files.readString and then verifySafeHtml() re-opens the same file with a new FileInputStream and parses it again into a PropertyResourceBundle, causing double I/O and double parse per file

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), the diff shows it reads the properties file once via Files.readString(file.toPath()) to run verifyNoDuplicateKeys(contents), then immediately calls verifySafeHtml(), which re-opens the same file with new FileInputStream(file) and parses it into a PropertyResourceBundle. This is verifiably double I/O and double parsing per file, but it’s a performance/efficiency concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Quadratic-ish anchor stripping in santizeAnchors: each loop iteration calls Pattern.quote + replaceFirst which compiles a fresh regex and rebuilds the string, and replaceFirst only removes the first occurrence so duplicate identical anchor tags (e.g., two identical <a href="{0}"> links) are never removed and matcher/value indices desynchronize

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, the loop iterates once per anchor-tag match from the original `value` (`matcher.find()`), and on each successful comparison it calls `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")`. Even if there are duplicate identical anchor tags, subsequent iterations will still remove the next remaining occurrence (after the first is removed), so the claim that duplicates are “never removed” is not supported by the diff. Also, the method does not use matcher indices, only `group()`, so “matcher/value indices desynchronize” is not a verifiable failure mode from the shown code. While each `replaceFirst` does rebuild the string and uses a regex each time, that’s a minor performance nit and not clearly important here given message-string sizes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-key regex re-execution in normalizeValue: replaceAll calls with static patterns (CLAIM\.<[A-Z]*>, <Extensions>, {n,choice,...}, and the quoted RTL style pattern) are re-compiled and executed for every key in every bundle even when the key cannot match; should pre-compile Pattern constants and gate on key name

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(), several String.replaceAll(...) calls use regex literals (e.g., "CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>", "<Extensions>", "\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", and a Pattern.quote(...) inside replaceAll for the RTL style). These regexes will be compiled each time normalizeValue is invoked per key/value during verifySafeHtml() iteration. While some are already gated by key equality/startsWith checks, they are still recompiled/executed per matching key and (for the email style removal) per value when the file path contains "email". Precompiling Patterns/constants would avoid repeated compilation; this is a performance/cleanliness concern, not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: English-file path derivation regex is fragile: replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties", "_en.properties") can mis-derive paths for directories containing _+suffix patterns, and any miss causes a FileNotFoundException wrapped in RuntimeException aborting the whole verification run; for _en files it needlessly re-derives and reopens its own path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` which derives an English bundle path via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` and then unconditionally opens it, throwing `RuntimeException` on `IOException`. From the code shown, any derivation miss or missing `_en.properties` file will abort verification rather than reporting a message. Also, when the current file is already `_en.properties`, the logic still re-derives and reopens essentially the same file. While this may be intended for strict verification, it is a concrete robustness/maintainability concern grounded in the diff rather than a proven functional defect for the shown paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IOException or unresolvable English fallback file in verifySafeHtml() throws bare RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, killing the build with poor diagnostics

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, both `PropertyResourceBundle` loads (`new FileInputStream(file)` and `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`) catch `IOException` and rethrow a bare `RuntimeException` ("unable to read file ..."). Since `verify()` only declares/throws `MojoExecutionException` and doesn’t catch these runtime exceptions, a missing/unresolvable derived English fallback path (or any read failure) will abort execution via unchecked exception rather than producing a controlled `MojoExecutionException` (or accumulating a message), matching the finding’s concern about build failure and poorer plugin-style diagnostics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: containsHtml uses lowercase-only regex <[a-z]+[^>]*>, so uppercase tags like <B> or <A HREF=...> are classified as no-HTML, causing legitimate translations to be stripped and flagged as Illegal HTML

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties, containsHtml() uses `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which matches only lowercase tag names. If an English source string contains HTML with uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g., `<B>`, `<A ...>`), containsHtml() would return false, leading to `POLICY_NO_HTML` and causing HTML in translations to be sanitized away and then reported as "Illegal HTML". This is a real correctness defect in the HTML-detection logic introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong-language content in translation files: messages_lt.properties totpStep1 replaced with Italian text, and messages_zh_CN.properties totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese text, not caught by the new verifier
santizeAnchors() mutates value while Matcher still references the original string, causing offset misalignment and removal of the wrong anchor tag occurrence in multi-anchor messages

adjudication.rationale: In santizeAnchors(), although `value` is reassigned via `replaceFirst(...)` inside the `while (matcher.find())` loop, the code never uses matcher indices/offsets (e.g., `start()`/`end()`) to remove at a specific position. It simply removes the first occurrence of the exact matched anchor-tag string (`englishMatcher.group()`) each iteration. Since the loop processes tags in order and only removes (never inserts) anchor tags, there is no demonstrated “offset misalignment” bug in the diff that would cause removing the wrong occurrence specifically due to matcher offsets. The finding’s stated mechanism isn’t supported by what the code does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error-path inconsistency: verifySafeHtml uses RuntimeException while verify() uses MojoExecutionException for the same failure class

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, verify() wraps file read IOExceptions into MojoExecutionException, but the newly added verifySafeHtml() reads both the current file and the derived English file via FileInputStream and on IOException throws a RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). Since verifySafeHtml() is invoked inside verify() without catching RuntimeException, the method can now fail with an unchecked exception for the same class of I/O failures that verify() otherwise reports as MojoExecutionException, changing/breaking the intended error-reporting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-file detection via file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email") is fragile and can silently strip RTL style attributes from all keys in unrelated paths containing 'email'

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue`, the new logic checks `if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email"))` and then strips the literal ` style="direction: rtl;"` from *all* message values in that file. This is indeed a fragile path heuristic: any non-email properties file whose absolute path happens to contain the substring `email` would get this normalization, potentially hiding differences/illegal HTML that the verifier is supposed to report. The diff doesn’t show an actual affected unrelated path, so it’s an edge-case robustness issue rather than a demonstrably failing behavior in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the positive path where the English source contains allowed HTML and translation legitimately contains the same HTML (POLICY_SOME_HTML branch and anchor pass-through), so a bug stripping/rejecting legitimate HTML would only surface as a build failure

adjudication.rationale:
The new HTML verification logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` has a distinct “allowed HTML” path: it selects `POLICY_SOME_HTML` when `containsHtml(englishValue)` is true and it has special handling to permit matching `` tags via `santizeAnchors(...)`. The added tests (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) only assert negative cases (they all expect an error message like "Illegal HTML" or "Didn't find anchor tag") and there is no test that asserts the positive case where the English string contains allowed HTML and a translation contains the same allowed HTML / same anchor tags and therefore should produce no findings. This makes it possible for a regression in the permissive branch (e.g., mistakenly flagging valid `
`, `

`, `/`, or matching anchors) to go untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Workaround/normalization paths in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, error-invalid-multivalued-size special cases, email RTL style stripping, double unescapeHtml4, '<!-- -->' removal) have zero test coverage and may silently break when the OWASP sanitizer library is upgraded

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new normalization/sanitization logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` and `normalizeValue()` with multiple key-specific and path-specific workarounds (e.g., `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `{choice...}` replacement for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, email `style="direction: rtl;"` stripping, plus post-sanitize `unescapeHtml4` and `<!-- -->` removal). The new tests only cover duplicate keys, a generic illegal HTML tag, disallowing HTML when English has none, and changed anchors; none of the added fixtures use those special keys or an email-path file, so those branches/workarounds are not exercised. That makes the concern about these special-case paths lacking test coverage diff-grounded and actionable, without being a direct functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error path where a translation file has no _en counterpart throws a raw RuntimeException (instead of MojoExecutionException) and is untested, risking a build crash with an unhelpful exception on unmapped paths

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, the English counterpart is opened via `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` where `englishFile` is derived by string replacements. If that file does not exist (or path mapping is wrong), the `catch (IOException e)` block throws a raw `RuntimeException` (`"unable to read file" + englishFile`) rather than a `MojoExecutionException`, and this exception is not caught in `verify()` (which only catches `IOException` around `Files.readString(...)`). This can crash the build with an unexpected exception type and less structured reporting. The added tests do not cover the missing-English-file scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong-language translations shipped: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text and zh_CN totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese text; the theme-verifier HTML check cannot detect wrong-locale content and no test or review gate covers it

adjudication.rationale: The diff directly changes Lithuanian strings to Italian: `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties` sets `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` and `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` sets `loginTotpStep1` to the same Italian text. It also changes `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties` `totpStep1` to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese wording in a zh_CN (Simplified) file. These are wrong-locale translations being shipped, which is a concrete, verifiable defect. The added theme-verifier logic only checks HTML safety/anchors and does not address locale/language correctness, consistent with the finding’s second point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-key test assertion loosened from Matchers.contains to Matchers.hasItem, so the test passes even if the new HTML check emits spurious additional messages on the duplicate-keys fixture, masking defects

adjudication.rationale: The diff does loosen the duplicate-keys test: it changes the assertion from `Matchers.contains(Matchers.containsString("Duplicate keys in file"))` (which requires the list to contain exactly one matching element in that order) to `Matchers.hasItem(Matchers.containsString("Duplicate keys in file"))` (which allows additional messages). Since `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()` now also runs `verifySafeHtml()`, the test no longer fails if extra verifier messages are produced for the same fixture, reducing the test’s ability to detect unexpected additional findings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New pluralization MessageFormat choice pattern ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}) in messages_en.properties and account-ui equivalent is untested and never rendered with 0/1/2+ values to verify correct output

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a MessageFormat choice pattern for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in several `messages*_en.properties` files, but the PR contains no code path or tests related to *rendering* these messages with 0/1/2+ values. The added/updated tests in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` only assert duplicate keys and HTML-sanitization behavior, not message formatting. Therefore the finding’s claim that the pattern is “never rendered with 0/1/2+ values” (and that this should be tested) is not something that can be verified from the diff alone; it’s speculative rather than diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Brittle path-based coupling: English source file located by regex string-munging of getAbsolutePath() ('resources-community'→'resources', '_xx.properties'→'_en.properties'), silently no-ops or crashes if file lives outside expected layout — path derivation should come from mojo configuration instead

adjudication.rationale: The new verifySafeHtml() derives the English bundle path via getAbsolutePath() string munging: `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` and `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`, then unconditionally opens it with FileInputStream and throws a RuntimeException on IOException. This is a diff-grounded fragility/tight coupling to a specific repository layout and filename convention; running the verifier on files outside that layout (or where the English counterpart isn’t present at the derived path) will fail. However, the diff doesn’t prove that such files exist in the intended execution scope, so it’s more an architectural/robustness issue than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Key-specific special cases hardcoded in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHack, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) whitelist exact keys inside generic HTML verification, growing list and breaking silently on key renames — should use declaration-based mechanism

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds HTML verification with `normalizeValue(key, value)` containing hardcoded key-based exceptions: `key.equals("templateHelp")`, `key.equals("optimizeLookupHelp")`, and `key.startsWith("linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit") || key.equals("error-invalid-multivalued-size")` to strip/replace patterns before sanitization. This embeds a growing whitelist of exact message keys inside a generic verifier; if those keys are renamed/duplicated elsewhere, the verifier behavior changes silently (exceptions won’t apply), which is a maintainability/architecture concern rather than an immediate functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric entity unescaping (unescape before sanitize and again after) can mask real problems: benign values with literal & or numeric entities may normalize differently and produce false 'Illegal HTML' failures; fragile escape/unescape dance already leaking into per-value hacks like <!-- --> removal

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `normalizeValue()` unescapes HTML entities before sanitization (`StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)`), and `verifySafeHtml()` unescapes again after OWASP sanitization (`unescapeHtml4(sanitized)`) plus applies ad-hoc cleanup (`sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")`). This escape/unescape roundtrip is indeed fragile and can change what is being sanitized/compared (e.g., `<...>` becomes a real `<...>` tag before the policy check), which can lead to surprising “Illegal HTML” reports and necessitates per-key hacks (e.g., replacing choice formats, stripping `style="direction: rtl;"`). However, from the diff alone it’s not provable that this causes incorrect behavior in practice (it may be intentional to prevent entity-based HTML bypass), so it’s better framed as a robustness/maintainability concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml throws bare RuntimeException('unable to read file...') instead of wrapping in MojoExecutionException like existing verify() error handling, surfacing as unhandled runtime crash

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), only IOException from Files.readString/verifyNoDuplicateKeys/verifySafeHtml is caught and wrapped into MojoExecutionException. However, verifySafeHtml() catches IOException when reading the properties bundles (new FileInputStream(file)/englishFile) and rethrows a bare RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). That unchecked exception will bypass the verify() IOException handler and can crash the mojo instead of producing a MojoExecutionException like the existing error-handling pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
containsHtml regex HTML_TAGS '<[a-z]+[^>]*>' misses uppercase tags like ,

,
, causing false POLICY_NO_HTML positives depending on case — use case-insensitive flag

adjudication.rationale:
In `VerifyMessageProperties`, `containsHtml()` uses `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which only matches lowercase tag names. If an English source string contains uppercase HTML tags (e.g., ``, `

`, `
`), `containsHtml(englishValue)` will incorrectly return false, causing `POLICY_NO_HTML` to be applied and potentially flag/strip HTML in translations even though the source contains HTML. This logic is introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors uses replaceFirst on Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), removing first occurrence of identical tag which may not be the matched occurrence — position-insensitive logic in a position-sensitive check; method name also misspelled ('santizeAnchors')
POLICY_SOME_HTML / POLICY_NO_HTML are non-static, package-visible mutable instance fields re-initialized per verification instead of private static final constants

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties, the policies are declared as `PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = ...` and `PolicyFactory POLICY_NO_HTML = ...` (no access modifier, not `final`, not `static`). That makes them package-visible, mutable instance fields, even though they appear to be immutable constants used for sanitization policy selection. Making them `private static final` would better express intent and avoid per-instance construction. The finding’s “re-initialized per verification” phrasing is a bit off (they’re initialized per instance, not per `verify()` call), but the core issue is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML can be smuggled inside {n,choice,...} clauses for allowlisted keys: normalizeValue replaces ChoiceFormat clauses with '...' in both translation and English source before sanitization, so dangerous markup in choice branches passes the sanitized-vs-original comparison and is rendered at runtime (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(), for keys starting with "linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit" or equal to "error-invalid-multivalued-size", the code replaces any MessageFormat choice clause ("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}") with "..." before sanitization/comparison. This means any HTML injected inside the choice branches would be removed from both the translated value and the English value prior to POLICY_* sanitization, so the later `if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value))` check cannot detect it. The finding correctly points out a bypass in the new HTML verification logic introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same smuggled-content hole exists for templateHelp CLAIM.<[A-Z]*> and optimizeLookupHelp <Extensions> strips, though with narrower scope (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue()`, special-casing strips tag-like substrings before sanitization: for `templateHelp` it removes `CLAIM\.<[A-Z]*>` and for `optimizeLookupHelp` it removes literal ``. Because this happens *prior* to `policy.sanitize(value)`, a translation could include real HTML elements that match these patterns (e.g., `CLAIM.`), which would be removed from `value` and therefore never detected as illegal HTML by the verifier, defeating the safety check. This is a verifiable bypass introduced by the new normalization logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile English-file path derivation in verifySafeHtml: the greedy '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' regex is applied to the whole absolute path, so earlier underscores in CI workspace/home/temp dir paths get rewritten, producing a nonexistent path and crashing the build instead of degrading gracefully (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In verifySafeHtml(), the English file path is derived via file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties"). The locale-suffix regex cannot match “earlier underscores in CI workspace/home/temp dir paths” unless that same path segment also contains “.properties”, because the character class [a-zA-Z-_]* does not include path separators (/ or \\) and thus cannot span directories. In normal paths, only the filename segment ends with .properties, so only the filename’s locale suffix is affected. The claimed failure mode (rewriting earlier underscores leading to a nonexistent path) is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the English properties file is missing/moved, aborting verification of all remaining checks instead of reporting a diagnostic; getEnglishValue fallback only handles missing keys, not missing files (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the code derives an English properties path (englishFile = file.getAbsolutePath()..._en.properties) and then loads it with new FileInputStream(englishFile). If that file is missing/moved, the catch (IOException e) throws a raw RuntimeException("unable to read file ...", e). This RuntimeException is not handled by verify() (which only catches IOException around Files.readString), so verification aborts instead of returning a diagnostic message. getEnglishValue() only handles MissingResourceException for missing keys, not a missing English file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Italian text committed into Lithuanian translation file messages_lt.properties, key totpStep1: wrong-language content shipped to users (P2)
matched_golden_ids: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that Italian text was committed in the Lithuanian locale file (messages_lt.properties) and should not be there, which is the same underlying problem as the golden comment (needs Lithuanian translation instead of Italian).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式, 驗證碼) committed into the Simplified Chinese zh_CN file messages_zh_CN.properties, key totpStep1: locale/script mismatch (P2)
matched_golden_ids: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag that the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) translation for key totpStep1 contains Traditional Chinese wording/characters, indicating a locale/script mismatch that should be verified/corrected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Path-based 'email' substring heuristic in normalizeValue strips style="direction: rtl;" from any file whose path merely contains 'email', allowing translators to inject RTL styles in unrelated files whose English source lacks them; broaden the anchor/attribute equality rule instead (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue(), the RTL style is removed based solely on `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` and not on message key/content ("// TODO: move the RTL information for emails"). This makes the exception path-based and potentially overly broad: any properties file whose path happens to include the substring "email" will have ` style="direction: rtl;"` ignored by the verifier (for both source and translation via normalizeValue calls), which is a brittle/scoping concern created by this diff. The finding’s mention of changing the anchor/attribute equality rule is not directly supported by the diff, but the core point about the path-substring heuristic is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor-violation message in santizeAnchors omits the file name, making violations hard to localize across thousands of properties files (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(...)`, the violation message added on mismatch is `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")`, which omits both the `file` and the `key`. Given this verifier runs across many `.properties` files, the output would be hard to localize compared to other messages in this class (e.g., `Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded diagnostics/usability issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Method name misspelled as santizeAnchors instead of sanitizeAnchors (cosmetic) (P3)
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out the same typo in the method name: 'santizeAnchors' is missing the 'i' and should be 'sanitizeAnchors'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException on I/O errors instead of MojoExecutionException, bypassing the plugin's error-handling convention and making failure messages inconsistent (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), only the initial Files.readString(...) I/O is wrapped and converted to MojoExecutionException. The newly added verifySafeHtml() reads both the target file and the derived English file via FileInputStream and on IOException it throws a raw RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). That unchecked exception can now escape verify() (despite its MojoExecutionException contract) and bypass consistent Maven plugin error handling/messages.
